---
title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Pest Control"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    standalone: true
---

Biological pest control is valued as the extra yield natural enemies provide on organically
managed cropland, at the organic producer price. The base year is 2019.

The scope is organic agriculture only, by design: the underlying evidence measures the yield
effect of predators where synthetic pesticides are absent, and no comparable estimate exists
for conventional systems. The full value is attributed to nature, with no human-input share
taken out (λ = 1), unlike the neighbouring crop rows.

## Source

The write-up is `Pest_Control.docx` (26 October 2026) in the shared folder of current write-ups.
The effect sizes are Boldorini et al. (2024), Table S3. The authors' current scripts are not yet
received, so the library follows the write-up's appendix where it can and departs from it in
the three places listed under What is open.

## Quantity

Organic production per crop and country: FiBL's organic area extract, times the country's
conventional FAOSTAT yield, times an organic-to-conventional yield ratio per FAO crop group
(`pest_control_yield_ratio_*`). FiBL aggregate rows with no FAOSTAT production analogue are
excluded and their share logged, never guessed.

## Price

The organic producer price: the country's FAOSTAT 2019 producer price for the crop (the item's
global median where the country reports none), times the organic-to-conventional price premium
(`pest_control_price_premium`).

Where FAOSTAT reports no yield or producer price for a crop and country that FiBL gives organic
area, the missing factor is imputed with the global median across the countries that do report
it for the same crop, so a real organic area is not dropped for want of a price. A country
missing every factor stays missing rather than imputed into existence.

## Valuation

Per crop $i$, country $j$:

$$
\text{Value}_{ij} = \left(e^{\text{lnRR}_{g(i)}} - 1\right) \; A_{ij} \; y_{ij} \, r_{g(i)} \; p_{ij} \, \pi
$$

where $\text{lnRR}_{g(i)}$ is the crop group's meta-analytic log response ratio
(`pest_control_effect_lnrr_*`: the cereal effect for cereals, the vegetable effect for
vegetables, oilseeds and pulses, the other-crops effect for fruit, nuts and stimulants, zero
for every other group), $A$ the organic area, $y$ the conventional yield, $r$ the yield ratio,
$p$ the producer price and $\pi$ the price premium, 1.38. Countries sum over crops, and the
published table carries all 250 account countries with NA where nothing is valued.

The committed `pest_control_gep.csv` is carried beside the result as the comparison anchor. It
is a Monte Carlo mean from a pipeline that is not on the drive, so the run log reports coverage
and the Pearson correlation of log values over the countries both tables value, rather than a
to-the-cent match. The total scales linearly in $\pi$. On the
132 countries both tables value, the library's total is 3.4% above the committed one at
$\pi = 1.38$, and 25% below it at $\pi = 1$.

## Coverage

The published table is one row for each of the account's 250 countries, base year 2019, in 2019
USD. Of the 250, 138 carry a value, totalling \$6,467,213,436.55, 2 are computed zeros (Mali and
Tajikistan), and 110 rows are missing, kept as missing rather than zero because an input carries
no data for those countries. A zero means the computation returned zero. A missing row means
the data to compute one is absent. The library values eight countries the committed table does
not (AND, GIN, GMB, LIE, MLI, MUS, REU, TJK).

## Inputs

All paths and parameters come from `es_parameters.csv` under the `pest_control` service key:
the FiBL area extract, the FAOSTAT 2019 yield and price slices, the FAO/CPC crop
classification, the three effect sizes, the six yield ratios, the price premium and the
committed reference, each with a source row beside it.

## Output

`gep_calculation` writes `gep_by_country_base_year.csv` into its own task directory, holding the
r250 identifiers and attributes, `year`, `pest_control_gep` and `pest_control_gep_reference`,
and `pest_control_by_crop_country.csv` beside it with the per-crop rows.

## What is open

The write-up differs from the implementation in three places, and alignment waits on the
authors' cleaned scripts:

- Cereals. The write-up leaves them unvalued because their effect is not significantly different
  from zero. The library values them at the cereal effect, \$718,037,931.97 over 79 countries,
  11.1% of the total.
- Missing prices and yields. The write-up imputes them with a mixed-effects model on log prices.
  The library takes the crop's global median.
- The price premium. The write-up uses a ratio per crop from matched USDA GATS pairs, with the
  FAO crop group's mean as the fallback. The library applies the overall mean, 1.38, to every
  crop.
